title: Autonomous 3D Visual-Thermal Inspection for Utility-Scale Solar Farms

problem.summary: Utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) inspection is dominated by aerial surveys, which are effective for identifying module-level hot cells but provide limited visibility of critical components located under the array, including connectors, cabling, fasteners and structural elements.
statements: Utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) inspection is dominated by aerial surveys, which are effective for identifying module-level hot cells but provide limited visibility of critical components located under the array, including connectors, cabling, fasteners and structural elements.
These assets are difficult to inspect consistently at scale, and their defects are often spatially small, partially occluded and difficult to localise from isolated images.
We present an automated 3D visual-thermal inspection system (Tricorder ) for under-panel PV asset inspection.

We present an automated 3D visual-thermal inspection system (Tricorder ) for under-panel PV asset inspection.
The approach combines LiDAR-inertial Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) with geometrically calibrated RGB and thermal imagery and machine-learning-based object detection and segmentation.

limitations.summary: However, many critical electrical and structural failure points, including MC4 connectors, cabling, fasteners, and mounting components, are located beneath the modules and are difficult to observe from above.
items: However, many critical electrical and structural failure points, including MC4 connectors, cabling, fasteners, and mounting components, are located beneath the modules and are difficult to observe from above.
Inspecting these components, therefore, remains dependent on labour-intensive hand-held inspection.
The challenge is not only detecting these assets, but determining what component is being observed, its condition, and where it is located in 3D space.

deploymentClaims: Field Deployment and Experimental Evaluation Field data were collected at CSIRO's Photovoltaic Outdoor Research Facility in Newcastle, and three commercial utility-scale PV solar farms around Australia.

These deployments capture substantial variation in PV structure, component configuration, illumination, weathering, corrosion and background clutter, providing representative data for developing and evaluating under-panel asset detection and defect-identification methods.
